basis: The Scuola Normale author profile lists the thesis and the review under one person; its research report identifies that review as the H-Net review on the other key.

evidence.says: Andrea S. Watkins of Northern Kentucky University earned a 1999 Kentucky PhD, worked on Robert Wickliffe and his family, and recommended Slavery's Borderland.

basis: The reviewer's Northern Kentucky affiliation and the 1999 doctorate match the association profile, which also identifies the specific family studied in the dissertation and names a book reviewed on the other key. The connection is inferred rather than an explicit listing of the dissertation title.

evidence.says: Andrew Boeger of North Carolina A&T State University reviewed They Eat from Their Labor for H-LatAm in 1996.
Andrew Boeger earned a 1994 UT Austin history doctorate with a dissertation on community control at Bolivia's Chojlla mine, 1944–1964.
A 1996 conference program lists Andrew Boeger of North Carolina A&T presenting on Bolivian mine workers, 1944–1964.

basis: The reviewer's affiliation matches the conference speaker's, and the dissertation and paper concern the same period. No source found explicitly connects the dissertation author to that institution or names both works, so the evidence does not meet the required identity standard.

evidence.says: Andrew Nurse's CV lists his Queen's PhD dissertation, Tradition and Modernity: The Cultural Work of Marius Barbeau, and his 2005 H-Canada publication Canadianization.

basis: Mount Allison's faculty CV lists the dissertation and the H-Canada review under the same scholar. It dates the dissertation to 1997, while the graph records 1998.

evidence.says: Lists Anna Manchin as the H-Net reviewer of Invented Lives, Imagined Communities.
Brown lists Anna B. Manchin and the 2008 dissertation Fables of Modernity: Entertainment Films and the Social Imaginary in Interwar Hungary.

basis: The sources identify the reviewer and the dissertation author, but do not establish a link between them. The shared name and compatible subject are insufficient to merge the keys.

evidence.says: Benjamin Gross says he works at Linda Hall Library; his author note describes his Princeton PhD dissertation on the first LCDs at RCA.
Princeton lists Benjamin Gross's 2011 dissertation as Crystallizing Innovation: The Emergence of the LCD at RCA, 1951-1976.

basis: The review credit places Benjamin Gross at Linda Hall Library. His IEEE article identifies a Linda Hall employee whose Princeton dissertation matches the dissertation listed on the other key in institution and subject; Princeton supplies its title and year.

evidence.says: Benjamin Lammers of Caldwell College's history and political science department reviewed Gender, Modernity, and the Popular Press in Inter-War Britain in 2007.
Benjamin Lammers has a Rutgers University Ph.D. and has taught history at Caldwell since 1999.
Cites Benjamin Lammers's A Superior Kind of English: Jewish Ethnicity and English Identity in London's East End, 1905–1939 as a 1997 Rutgers Ph.D. dissertation.

basis: The 2007 review identifies its author at Caldwell, whose faculty page gives Benjamin Lammers a Rutgers doctorate. A scholarly citation identifies the matching 1997 dissertation as a Rutgers Ph.D., making the identity a strong career inference.

evidence.says: Boris DeWiel's CV lists a University of Calgary PhD in political science in 1998 and UNBC appointments beginning in 2000.
Boris DeWiel is a UNBC political science professor who joined its faculty in 2000 and completed his PhD in 1998 at Calgary.

basis: The UNBC professor's CV places him at Calgary for his doctorate in 1998 and at UNBC from 2000, matching the two review credits in 1997 and 2001. The matching institutions and dates support one career.

evidence.says: Brad Wright is at Kennesaw State, holds a Middle Tennessee State PhD in public history, and is writing a book titled Counternarratives of Doña Lucha.
Brad H. Wright submitted The Counternarratives of Doña Lucha as a Middle Tennessee State University public history dissertation in 2020.

basis: The Kennesaw State scholar is identified with the same distinctive dissertation project and the same degree and university as the thesis author. The review credit independently places Brad Wright at Kennesaw State in 2022.

evidence.says: Brent M. S. Campney's CV lists his reviews of Swift to Wrath (2014) and Forgotten Dead (2015).

basis: Campney's university-hosted CV lists a review from each key under the same scholar.

evidence.says: Brian J. McVeigh's CV lists reviews of Globalisation and the Asia-Pacific and World-Systems Analysis, and his University of Arizona post in 2003–2013.

basis: McVeigh's CV lists reviews of works on both keys under his name, and his Arizona appointment matches the first key's review-credit affiliation. The CV gives a different year for the Globalisation review than the queue record, but the title and review venue match.

evidence.says: Brian Becker of Delta State earned a Ph.D. in medieval history at Western Michigan University in 2010 and published reviews in H-HRE, H-Maritime, and H-Italy.
In 2009 Western Michigan reported Brian Becker was completing a dissertation titled Life and Local Administration on Fifteenth Century Genoese Chios.

basis: The AHA record for b identifies a 2010 Western Michigan history doctorate, matching the degree and year of the Delta State reviewer on a. The university newsletter independently places Becker at Western Michigan working on a dissertation on Genoese Chios, though it gives a different title.

evidence.says: Brian Vick's CV lists him in Sheffield's history department in 2002–2007 and Colorado Boulder's history department in 2007–2008.

basis: The CV places one Brian Vick at the two institutions identified by the review credits during the corresponding years. The dated institutional sequence connects the two keys' careers.

evidence.says: Buffalo State professor Bridget Maria Chesterton has a Ph.D. from SUNY Stony Brook and lists the October 2021 H-Net review of Native Peoples, Politics, and Society.
Bridget María Chesterton is a Buffalo State history professor who received her doctorate at Stony Brook University in 2007.

basis: The reviewer's faculty page identifies her Stony Brook doctorate, and the 2007 degree year matches the thesis record; the named dissertation is recorded as a 2007 Stony Brook Ph.D. thesis. This career link supports the same person, although the faculty page does not name the dissertation.
